title: Write the Date
description: Fill the day, month and year boxes on a real card, spell the month in words or write it in numbers, and turn a date from one way into the other.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Say the day, the month and the year of a date, write a date with the month in words or in numbers as DD-MM-YYYY, and turn a date from one way into the other.
writeup.look: A real card with three rounded boxes for the day, the month and the year, a month ladder of twelve tiles with their numbers, a toggle between the month in words and in numbers, and a pad.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Write the Date' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: how many of the three boxes are filled. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The real card is a rounded card 560 by 300 at x 90, y 230, drawn as a birthday card, an invitation or a school notice in its natural colours with a line of words on it that names the event. The three rounded boxes stand in a row under the words at y 440: the day box 120 wide at x 130, the month box 220 wide at x 270 and the year box 160 wide at x 510, each 70 tall, with its label beneath in words, Day, Month and Year, so a part is told by its label before anything else. When the toggle is set to numbers, short dashes are drawn between the boxes. The month ladder is twelve tiles in two columns of six at x 740, y 232, each 150 by 54 with a 10 gap, each tile holding a month name and its number, January 01 down to December 12, and a tapped tile lights once. The month toggle is a button 300 by 64 at x 740, y 560 labelled Month in words and Month in numbers. A Check button stands under the card at x 90, y 580 (200 by 64), and a line in words under it says when a date is not a real one and why. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys and a clear key, for typing the day, the month number and the year into the answer slot. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Real objects keep their own natural colours. The hour hand of a clock is vermilion and the minute hand is deep blue, because a hand is a mark that stands for a number, and the hours are vermilion and the minutes deep blue everywhere else, in a digital time, a label and a tag. The a.m. half of a day, from midnight to noon, is sky blue and the p.m. half, from noon to midnight, is amber. The time reached, a length of time worked out, a converted amount and the answer are green. A clock face, rim and numbers are near-black on cream, anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey, and chrome never borrows one of the five. Each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a time is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The card shows the last date in its boxes, written both ways, with the day, the month and the year each under its label and the month lit once on the ladder.

writeup.delight: Two small surprises. On the second and third phases, the month name or number lifts off its tile on the ladder and slides across into the month box. On the fourth phase, the toggle flips the whole date over like a page, and the three boxes keep the same day, month and year on the other side.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet typed. On the first phase a real birthday card stands with its date written on it and three empty boxes under it, labelled Day, Month and Year. On the second a real invitation shows its three boxes filled in numbers, with the toggle set to the month in words. On the third a real school notice shows three empty boxes, the month ladder lit with its numbers, and the toggle set to the month in numbers. On the fourth a real diary page shows a date written in words at the left and an empty row of boxes at the right. One thing moves, once: the first box, or the toggle on the second and fourth phases, gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any date the calendar allows in the three boxes, turned between the month in words and the month in numbers with the toggle, with the month ladder lighting each month. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on the parts of a date, the month in words, the month in numbers with two digits, a date that cannot be real, and dates turned from numbers into words and back, each on a real card or ticket.
voiceLines: A card with a date on it, and three empty boxes. Let us write it down.
A date has three parts. Which is the day? Which is the month? Which is the year?
Write the day first. Then spell the month out. Then the year. Read it aloud.
Find the month on the ladder. Its number goes in the middle. Two digits, two digits, four digits.
Say the date the other way. Turn the toggle. Do both ways name one day?
A new card. What is its day, its month and its year?
Free play. Write any date, and turn it between words and numbers.
Look at the labels under the boxes. Which part goes where?
You wrote the date in words and in numbers, and both said the same day.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, no colour means good or bad. The miss empties the answer slot at once (every digit, every box, a picked choice), so it is empty through the traceback; the pad re-opens empty after it.
tracebacks: Phase 1: the tiles in a wrong box go back to the card, a right box stays green with a tick, and each box lights in turn with what fits in it (1 to 31, a month, 4 digits)
Phase 2: the typed boxes empty, a right box stays green with a tick, and the labels Day, Month, Year light in order with what fits in each

Phase 3: the typed boxes empty, a right box stays green with a tick, the labels light in order and each wrong box shows DD, MM or YYYY (or 1 to 31, a month, 4 digits); a note says when a date is not real (no month 13, April has 30 days) or a 0 goes in front

voice.opening: Dates are written on cards, tickets and notices.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play: pick a month, tap Day or Year to type, see the date both ways.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You wrote the date in words and in numbers, and both said the same day.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 3 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 3; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 3 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }
